physics_goals.quote: The HERMES experiment is collecting data on inclusive and semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering of polarised positrons from polarised targets of H, D, and He.
physics_goals.value: Collect inclusive and semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering data on polarised targets to give information on the spin structure of the nucleon

summary.plain: HERMES shot HERA's high-energy positron or electron beam through very thin, spin-polarised gas targets of hydrogen, deuterium and helium to study how the spins of quarks and gluons add up to the spin of the proton and neutron. It took data from 1995 to 2007.
summary.technical: HERMES: forward-angle spectrometer (tracking chambers on either side of a 1.3 T m dipole, RICH, calorimeter) in the HERA East hall measuring inclusive and semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering of 27.6 GeV polarised positrons/electrons on internal polarised H, D and 3He gas targets (1995-2005) and unpolarised targets with a recoil detector (2006-2007); quark helicity distributions, g1, transverse-spin asymmetries and GPDs via DVCS.
